speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Health (a) how many places for home care and centre-based care services for the elderly are there currently; (b) how many referrals for each of these services have been received by the Agency for Integrated Care in 2015; and (c) how many of these referrals have been turned down and what are the main reasons for turning them down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have also been working to increase awareness of home- and centre-based care so that seniors and their families can consider these services for their care arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Its role is to facilitate the placement of seniors needing home or community care services or other appropriate aged care services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Once a referral is received, AIC works with the seniors and their families to find the most appropriate service to meet their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Not all referrals for home or centre-based care services translate into actual take-up for a variety of reasons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Of the referrals that did not result in services being taken up, about half were because families opted for alternative care arrangements such as hiring a domestic helper.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Another reason for not taking up the service is seniors being readmitted to the hospital as their conditions were not stable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there a waiting list, therefore, for those people who are not going to change the referral, because the spaces and the type of care that they want are not available?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there a waiting list and is there a criterion in which those put on the waiting list can be bumped up if there is an urgent need?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, not all referrals, as I have said, eventually choose to take up the service.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some could be because they have got alternative care arrangements, domestic helpers; some because the seniors are re-admitted to hospitals; in fact, there are also some where the seniors are concurrently referred to multiple services, both home and community care service, while they actually only need one.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: During the year, there may be patients who are discharged from home care or day care because they no longer need the service, because the conditions have improved, they have alternative care arrangements, or they have passed away.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In 2015, about 3,800 home care clients and 1,200 daycare clients did not continue with the service, which frees up capacity for others who need the places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Thirdly, for day care services, seniors may not need to have the service every day.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They may take up the service three days a week.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, one day care place can serve more than one senior.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There is some wait time for day care.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The reason, really, is because of geographical imbalance between supply and demand.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In some places – for instance, the Central region, mature estates, ageing profile – it is not easy to find sites for new senior care centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Sometimes, it is also because of patients' preferences.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, they want a day care centre in a certain location for convenience's sake.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the meantime, for those who are waiting for day care places, AIC works with the patient as well as the families for interim care arrangements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They can get on either to the home care services available or they can avail themselves of the Interim Caregiver Service (ICS).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When the senior is discharged from hospital, we can offer ICS whilst they are waiting for longer-term care arrangements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: ICS can be for a period of two weeks, in the first instance, and up to three months while they are waiting for longer-term care arrangements.
